author_prompt:
Author 8 DIFFERENT natural ecommerce customer-service dialogue families in en.
Batch 3; ensure at least four current turns classified as billing_refund across this batch.
Each family has its OWN coherent history of 2, 4 or 6 short alternating user/assistant
messages, followed by 3 ALTERNATIVE current user turns, not three sequential turns.
Those alternatives differ in effective intent: retain vs replace, withdraw vs
continue, single goal vs concurrent goal, or resolved vs unresolved reference.
Include natural short answers where history matters. Vary old completed tasks,
hesitation, self-correction, indirect wording, topics and dialogue acts. General
and human-service requests must also occur as NEW goals, not only stale history.
Do not follow a repeated sentence template or substitute product nouns to create
new families. Avoid stereotyped 'information only, do not submit' repetition.
Invent broad everyday ecommerce situations; no copied benchmark or private data.
History plus current turn should fit 150 English words or 180 Chinese characters;
keep it compact but meaningful. No future replies or final conversation summaries.
Supply the correct label for each alternative according to the rubric.

families.scenario: Customer asks about a smartwatch they bought that won't sync with their phone, then requests a refund.

messages.content: My FitPulse X2 arrived yesterday but it won't pair with my Android phone at all.
I'm sorry to hear that. Have you tried resetting the watch by holding the side button for 10 seconds?
Yeah, I did that twice. Still nothing. The Bluetooth just keeps dropping.
That's frustrating. Since it's within the 30-day window, we can offer a replacement unit or a full refund. Which would you prefer?
Honestly, I've lost confidence in this model. I'd rather just get my money back.

variants.text: Great, please process the refund to my original card.
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Actually, wait — could you first tell me if the newer X3 model has better Bluetooth range?
variants.label: product_technical

variants.text: Before we do that, can you check if my order was even charged correctly? I think I was double-billed.
variants.label: billing_refund

families.scenario: Customer's package was marked delivered but they never received it.

messages.content: My order #88412 says delivered yesterday but I never got it. The photo shows a porch but I don't have a porch.
That's concerning. Let me look into the delivery details for order #88412.
Thanks. Also, I noticed the tracking shows it was left at a neighbor's address in a different city.
I see that now. The carrier appears to have misrouted it. I can file a claim on your behalf.

variants.text: Please file the claim. And if it's truly lost, I want a refund, not a reshipment.
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Okay, but first — is my account showing the correct shipping address? I moved last month.
variants.label: account_security

variants.text: Actually, forget the claim. I just realized my cousin in that city might have picked it up. Let me call them first.
variants.label: __DEFER__

families.scenario: Customer wants to return a lamp that doesn't match their decor.

messages.content: I bought the Arc Floor Lamp last week and it's just too industrial-looking for my living room.
I understand. Returns are accepted within 60 days as long as the item is in original condition. Would you like to start a return?
Yes, but I threw away the box. Is that a problem?
Not at all. We can send you a prepaid label and you can use any sturdy box for shipping.

variants.text: Perfect, send me the label. Also, will the refund include the original shipping fee I paid?
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Great. By the way, do you carry a warmer-toned pendant light that would fit a mid-century style?
variants.label: product_technical

variants.text: Hmm, actually maybe I should keep it and just get different bulbs. What warm bulbs fit this model?
variants.label: product_technical

families.scenario: Customer's subscription order was renewed but they wanted to cancel.

messages.content: I thought I cancelled my coffee subscription last month, but I just got charged $39.99 again.
Let me check your subscription status. Can you confirm the email on your account?
It's j.martinez@mail.com. I definitely clicked cancel — I remember getting a confirmation screen.
I see that the cancellation didn't go through on our end. I apologize for the confusion. I can reverse the charge and cancel the subscription now.

variants.text: Yes, please reverse the charge and cancel it. I don't want any more shipments.
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Wait, before you cancel — can you tell me what roast is coming next month? I might keep it if it's the dark roast.
variants.label: product_technical

variants.text: Actually, I need to talk to a real person about this. I've been charged three times this year for things I cancelled.
variants.label: human_service

families.scenario: Customer asks about warranty coverage for a blender that stopped working.

messages.content: My BlendPro 500 stopped spinning after two months. The motor sounds like it's struggling.
That sounds like a motor issue. The BlendPro 500 has a 1-year warranty covering motor defects.
Good. So what's the process — do I send it in for repair or get a replacement?
We'll send you a replacement unit first, and you return the defective one with the prepaid label. No charge to you.

variants.text: That works. But I bought it with a gift card — will the replacement affect anything on that?
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Okay, send the replacement. Also, is there a quieter model you'd recommend for early mornings?
variants.label: product_technical

variants.text: Actually, I'd rather just get a refund instead of a replacement. I'm tired of this brand.
variants.label: billing_refund

families.scenario: Customer's login isn't working after a password reset.

messages.content: I can't log in. I requested a password reset but the link in the email expired before I clicked it.
No problem. I can send a fresh reset link to your registered email. Would you like me to do that?
Yes, please. And can you make sure my phone number is still on file for two-factor codes?
I've sent a new reset link and confirmed your phone number ending in 4421 is on file for 2FA.

variants.text: Thanks, got the link and I'm back in. Appreciate the quick help!
variants.label: general

variants.text: Got it. Now, about my last order — the delivery date got pushed back twice. What's going on?
variants.label: order_logistics

variants.text: Actually, I don't recognize that phone number ending in 4421. That's not mine. Someone may have accessed my account.
variants.label: account_security

families.scenario: Customer received a damaged ceramic vase and wants to discuss options.

messages.content: My vase from order #55210 arrived cracked. The box looked fine but the vase has a hairline fracture.
I'm sorry about that. We can send a replacement or issue a refund. Which option works better for you?
I was really excited about this vase for my dining table. Is the replacement from the same batch?
The replacement would come from our current stock, which is the same artisan batch as yours.

variants.text: Then send the replacement, please. And I'd like a small discount for the hassle — can you do 15% off?
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Actually, you know what, I'll just take the refund. I found a similar one at a local shop.
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Great, send it. Oh, and while you're at it — do you sell matching coasters from that same artisan?
variants.label: product_technical

families.scenario: Customer is checking on a backordered item and mentions a past issue.

messages.content: Hi, I'm just checking on my backordered desk chair. It's been three weeks now.
Let me check the status. The manufacturer said they'd ship by the end of this week.
Okay, that's what they said two weeks ago too. I'm getting a bit impatient.
I understand. I can escalate this to our supplier team to get a firmer date, or offer to cancel and refund if you'd prefer.

variants.text: Please escalate it. I'll wait a bit longer since I really like this chair.
variants.label: order_logistics

variants.text: You know what, just cancel it and refund me. I'll buy something else.
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Escalate it, but also — is there a similar ergonomic chair in stock that ships immediately?
variants.label: product_technical
